scenes.title: dbt Packages & Deployment
scenes.narration: This lesson covers dbt packages for reusing community code and the patterns for deploying dbt reliably to production.

scenes.title: What packages give you
bullets: Share macros, models, and tests across projects
scenes.narration: Packages let you import macros, models, and tests that someone else has already written, so you avoid reinventing common logic. Popular libraries such as dbt_utils provide battle-tested helpers for things like surrogate keys and date spines. By pinning package versions you also guarantee that everyone builds against the same code, keeping results reproducible.

scenes.title: Declaring dependencies
scenes.code:
# packages.yml
packages:
  - package: dbt-labs/dbt_utils
    version: 1.1.1
  - package: calogica/dbt_expectations
    version: 0.10.1
scenes.narration: You declare packages in a packages file, naming each one and pinning an exact version. Here we bring in dbt_utils for general-purpose macros and dbt_expectations for a richer library of data tests. Pinning versions is important because it prevents a surprise upgrade from silently changing your build. Running dbt deps then downloads everything into your project.

scenes.title: Environments and promotion
steps: Develop in a personal dev schema
CI builds and tests on pull requests
scenes.narration: A mature deployment separates environments through dbt targets. Each developer builds into a personal development schema so nobody steps on each other. Continuous integration then builds and tests the changes automatically on every pull request. Only after that passes does the code get promoted to run against the production target, keeping production clean and trusted.

scenes.title: Two ways to run in production

left.heading: Scheduler / dbt Cloud
points: Managed jobs on a cron schedule

right.heading: Orchestrator
points: dbt runs as a step in Airflow or Dagster

scenes.narration: There are two common production patterns. A managed scheduler such as dbt Cloud runs your jobs on a cron schedule with built-in logging and alerting, which keeps operational overhead low. Alternatively, you invoke dbt as one step inside a broader orchestrator like Airflow or Dagster, which lets you coordinate the dbt run with upstream ingestion and Spark jobs and gives you fine-grained control over the whole pipeline.

scenes.text: Always pin package versions and run CI on pull requests so production only ever sees code that already built and passed its tests.
scenes.narration: The practice to enforce is always pinning package versions and running continuous integration on pull requests, so that production only ever executes code which has already built successfully and passed every test.
